issues.description:
## Context

During the MOB-967 PR gate for crucible PR #382 on 2026-07-08, `council-flow --execute` failed before launching any reviewer lanes.

Command shape:

```sh
operator-supervisor council-flow \
  --out-dir /Users/ericlitman/.local/state/crucible/operator-supervisor/mob934-recovery-20260708T1518/council-pr-382-r1 \
  --repo ericlitman/crucible \
  --pr 382 \
  --executor-model openai/codex \
  --caller-model openai/codex \
  --allow-unready \
  --execute \
  --include-report
```

The static lease probe generated claimed proofs for `/Users/ericlitman/projects/crucible`, but the council jobs expected lease identities for materialized worktrees under:

```text
/Users/ericlitman/.local/share/crucible/production-rollout/materialization-worktrees/controller-f7d243bddd97c268
```

All reviewer lanes were rejected with `static_lease_identity_mismatch`, leaving `council-report.json` in `no_authoritative_external_evidence`.

Artifacts:

* `/Users/ericlitman/.local/state/crucible/operator-supervisor/mob934-recovery-20260708T1518/council-pr-382-r1/council-flow.json`
* `/Users/ericlitman/.local/state/crucible/operator-supervisor/mob934-recovery-20260708T1518/council-pr-382-r1/council-report.json`

## Acceptance criteria

* `council-flow` static lease probing proves the same workspace identity that its scheduled reviewer jobs will launch against.
* Materialized PR review worktrees either get lease proofs generated after their path is known, or the scheduler uses a stable lease identity consistently across dry-run and execute.
* Admission failure text tells the operator whether to regenerate capacity, disable probing, or use another supported recovery path.
* Add a regression test that a PR-backed `council-flow` with materialization worktrees does not reject all lanes due to canonical-vs-materialized lease mismatch.

## Problem

During MOB-813 B2 PR #342 review-fix recovery, `fix-implementer-r10` failed before the worker launched. The scheduler accepted `pro16`, but crabbox rejected the static lease because the per-worktree lease was already claimed by the operator workspace while the installed controller attempted to claim the same static lease for its own repo root.

## Evidence

* Schedule result: `/Users/ericlitman/.local/state/crucible/operator-supervisor/mob813-config-driven-lane-behavior-b2-r1/runs/b2-config-surface-retrofits/fix-dispatch-runs/fix-implementer-r10/schedule-result.json`

## Expected

Fix-dispatch launches from the installed controller while materializing the operator workspace should use a consistent lease identity for the branch/operator workspace, matching the static-lease proof gathered during capacity/admission. A warm claimed per-worktree lease should not make the next worker launch fail because the crabrunner repo root is the installed controller.

## Acceptance Criteria

* A fix-dispatch job launched from the installed controller with `workspace_materialization_mode=git-worktree` and `materialize_workspace_from=<operator workspace>` uses the operator workspace lease identity when calling crabbox.
* Capacity/static-lease proof and the actual crabbox launch use the same repo/lease identity.
* Regression coverage reproduces the installed-controller + operator-workspace mismatch and fails before the fix.
* The failure class is surfaced as a named lease-identity mismatch if it happens, not generic `submit_or_worker_failure`.

## Source

Surfaced by MOB-813 B2 / PR #342 while resolving the post-fix council P2 from `council-flow-r2`.

issues.title: Crabrunner timeouts orphan crabbox/SSH process trees and misclassify controller hangs
issues.description:
## Context

A council-flow batch reported that running several PR-level council flows simultaneously could "saturate the fleet" and cause non-codex lanes on studio1 to hit the 31-minute hard timeout with empty output. The expected operating model is still 10 lanes per host, so this should not be treated as a legitimate capacity limit without stronger proof.

This is P2 because the failure can mislead the operator control surface: the local controller reported empty-output timeouts while at least one remote studio1 job had already completed successfully.

## Why still real

Live investigation on 2026-06-30 found stale local process state, not a host-capacity rejection:

* Several `crabbox run` processes and child `ssh` commands were still running for more than five hours under PPID 1 after their parent controller had timed out.
* The stale OpenSSH ControlMaster socket at `/tmp/crabbox-ssh-8221cbaf-%C` was still present and reported `Master running`.
* Direct SSH to studio1 returned immediately.
* A crabbox-style SSH command encountered `mux_client_request_session: session request failed: Session open refused by peer`, disabled multiplexing, and completed successfully.
* Updating the local crabbox binary to upstream `github.com/openclaw/crabbox v0.33.0` and running 10 concurrent static-host smokes against studio1 completed successfully, so the 10-lane target itself is plausible.

The remaining bug is in our controller/runner behavior around hard timeouts, process-tree cleanup, durable phase logging, and failure classification.

## Acceptance criteria

* A timeout of a `crabrunner`/`crabbox` controller invocation terminates the whole local process tree, including child `crabbox` and `ssh` processes, instead of leaving PPID-1 orphans.
* Crabrunner records which crabbox subcall phase is active (`submit`, `status`, `collect`, or setup) before invoking crabbox, with enough artifact path and timing information to diagnose a later hard timeout.
* Empty-output local controller timeouts are classified distinctly from remote worker timeouts so council/gate summaries do not imply the model lane itself timed out when the controller transport hung.
* Regression coverage exercises a hanging child/grandchild process and proves timeout cleanup reaches descendants.
* Regression coverage proves crabrunner emits a durable breadcrumb before a crabbox subcall can hang.
* A 10-way static-host smoke against studio1 passes after stale local process/mux cleanup.
* studio1 is restored to the default fleet after fix, review, and deploy.

## Verification

* Unit/regression tests for process-tree timeout cleanup and crabbox subcall breadcrumbs.
* Targeted runner tests for failure classification.
* Manual smoke: direct SSH and crabbox static-host command against studio1.
* Manual stress: 10 concurrent `crabbox run --provider ssh --target macos --static-host 100.122.53.89 ... --no-sync -- echo CRABBOX_STRESS_i` runs.
* Full decorrelated review cycle on the PR before merge/deploy.
* Deploy proof showing the controller skill copy and crabrunner fleet are refreshed, with studio1 back in the default host sequence.

## Source refs

* `skills/session-orchestrator/scripts/production-rollout.mjs` currently times out spawned controller commands without killing the full descendant process tree.
* `crabrunner/src/client.ts` currently invokes crabbox subcommands through `spawnSync` without a durable pre-call phase breadcrumb.
* Stale local evidence observed on pro14: orphaned `crabbox run` PIDs `74373`, `74374`, `74516`, `76541`, `83641`, `90728`; child ssh PIDs `74468`, `74470`, `74552`, `76574`, `83683`, `90779`; mux master PID `83468`.
* Remote counterexample: studio1 job `crabbox-council-20260630T162241.377Z-mobilyze-llc-symphony-ts-693-deepseek-studio1` completed with worker exit code 0 while the local lane timed out.

issues.title: Validation-trust proof contract: one run-proof object (worker→controller→closeout), leading slice of MOB-565
issues.description:
## Why this exists (the bandaid cascade it stops)

The validation-trust seam has been peeled one layer at a time: MOB-779 (closeout reads
the ledger) → exposed MOB-782 (ledger drops evidence) → MOB-787/788 (ledger item_id /
outcome mis-key/normalize) → MOB-785 (attribution wants a result-row the *existing*
workspace-sync proof doesn't feed) → MOB-637 (worker can't validate). Each fix relocated
the blocker to the next layer — the tell of a symptom, not a root.

Grounded root: one question — *"is this run validated + attributed?"* — is reconciled
across **\~8 proof artifacts** (validation-ledger, validation-process, workspace-sync,
schedule-result, materialization, pr-gate, closeout, work_attribution) and **3****
****derivations** (worker / controller-ledger / closeout re-derivation), tangled across the
god-files (`production-rollout.mjs` 14.6k + `adaptive-orchestrator.mjs` 7.1k LOC). Every
child ticket is "wire one more edge" in a graph that should be one node.

## Mandate

* **Do NOT fix the children (MOB-782/785/787/788/637) individually.** That is the bandaid
  cascade. They are symptoms of a fragmented proof model.
* Resolve them by conforming to **one run-proof object**: the worker + controller write it
  **once, with evidence**; closeout **consumes** it — no re-derivation, no pairwise
  artifact reconciliation.
* This is the **leading slice of the MOB-565 god-file decomposition** (paced to the
  GPT-5.6 ship, ~Thu 2026-07-09). Do the validation/attribution/closeout untangle as
  decomposition slice 1, designed against this contract — not as edge-patches now.

## Track-suppression boundary (the lever that stops regrowth)

New QA / council findings in the validation-trust seam **attach here** (subsumed by this
redesign); they are **not** filed as new Triage siblings. This extends MOB-567 (which
routes non-blocking findings to Triage) with *seam scoping*: when a redesign epic owns a
seam, findings in that seam point at the epic instead of spawning a new pile. This is what
keeps implementing the seam from re-growing the backlog.

## The one-page contract to define at the cut

* What a validated+attributed run asserts (per-command outcome + exit_code + stdout/stderr
  tail; workspace-sync sha; result-row; attribution) — carried **inline in one artifact**.
* Who writes each field (worker validation, controller re-run, attribution gate) and who
  reads it (closeout, once).
* Single artifact, single flow, single source of truth — replacing the ~8 today.

## The only contract-neutral standalone

**MOB-782's evidence *persistence* only** — and shrunk: "write the already-captured
stdout/stderr to the already-declared `log_path` (currently 0 bytes)." Drop the
ledger-shape and truncation-policy changes (those pre-decide the contract). Route it as
**trivial-tier / single-lane review, not crabbox-council**, framed as a *diagnostic**
**prerequisite* so the next dogfood failure is legible when the contract is designed. It
must not itself become a council run that manufactures new track residue.

## Source

2026-07-04 MOB-781 validation-trust-seam dogfood + this session's grounding.
Related: MOB-565 (keystone), MOB-567 (track→Triage), MOB-779 (done).

**L2 — issue-role selection (dominant, previously unfiled).** Every ID found in PR body/title/branch is treated as equally authoritative spec. Verified consequences from 2026-07-08 post-fix runs:

* Follow-up/TRACKED tickets judged as the spec: crucible#382 → MOB-980 after MOB-967's heading failed — aim-inverting (the tickets a PR marks TRACKED are precisely what it deferred), guaranteeing a 0%-met verdict; crucible#384 → MOB-940, which had **already shipped 12h earlier in PR #371**, imported via a salvage branch-name string quoted in the body.

issues.title: Respect cross-exam Track downgrades in council round records
issues.description:
## Context

During SYMPH-1032 / PR #711 review, `review-quality-ledger.mjs round-record` converted a cross-exam downgraded Track finding into a blocking council-loop round finding.

## Why still real

The council triage initially escalated fingerprint `src/review/plan-review.ts:275-285::906dec7aa2` as P2. The cross-exam artifact then returned:

* `blocking: []`
* target verdict `verdict: "CONFIRM"`, `severity: "TRACK"` for that fingerprint
* `concurred: true`

Despite that, `round-record` emitted:

```json
{
  "blocking": [
    { "fp": "src/review/plan-review.ts:275-285::906dec7aa2" }
  ],
  "cross_examined": true
}
```

This can incorrectly prevent `council-loop` convergence or merge readiness when a cross-examiner confirms a real issue but explicitly downgrades it to Track.

## Acceptance criteria

* `round-record` treats cross-exam-confirmed findings as blocking only when the final cross-exam severity remains P1/P2.
* Cross-exam `severity: TRACK` findings remain durable Track findings but do not populate the round `blocking` set.
* Add a regression test with triage P2, cross-exam `CONFIRM + severity TRACK`, and expected `blocking: []`.
* Preserve existing behavior for P1/P2 confirmed findings and for prior-round blocking inheritance.

## Verification

* Run the new `review-quality-ledger` regression test.
* Re-run a `round-record` command against the PR #711 artifact pair and verify the generated round record has `blocking: []`.

issues.title: Operator Supervisor CLI: one coherent front-door surface agents won't bypass
issues.description:
## Goal

A clean, consistent Operator Supervisor CLI that an agent/operator can drive a real multi-lane batch through **end to end, with no reason to go around it.** Today the front door (`operator-supervisor run/continue/status/doctor`) is a capability *subset* of the layer beneath it, mixes flags and env-vars, and can't start clean or show live state — so every real run spills into `node …/adaptive-orchestrator.mjs operator-run …` / `crabrunner …` and hand-managed files. That spill *is* the hand-driving MOB-645 set out to end.

## Evidence — four dogfoods, four bypasses

* **MOB-521/525/478** (this session): dropped to `continue --capacity-file` + hand-recovery; wrote a fresh `queue-v2` to dodge stale terminal items.
* **MOB-530/554** (this session): hand-validated + hand-merged (front door stops at implement).
* **MOB-558/704** (runbook D1): dropped to `operator-run … --validation-command` because `run` lacks the flag; avoided the default queue's stale blockers.
* **MOB-707** (Codex): dropped to raw `crabrunner run`/`status`; proved liveness by grepping `crabbox-calls.jsonl`; SIGINT'd an unbounded lane.

Four independent operators, one failure mode: the friendly surface isn't sufficient, so they fall into the verbose, inconsistent one.

## Design principles (the coherent surface)

1. **Superset, not subset.** Anything the operator path needs from `operator-run`/`crabrunner` is reachable via `operator-supervisor <verb>`. No capability forces a bypass.
2. **One entry, one style.** `operator-supervisor <verb>` is the only thing typed; one interface style (flags), no `SUPERVISOR_*` env-var wrapper; the tool's emitted `next_command` and the skill agree verbatim.
3. **Clean-slate + live.** A run can start fresh; `status` shows real lane liveness without opening low-level logs.
4. **Consistent vocabulary + safe defaults + fail-loud.** One name per concept; safe defaults (timeouts); never exit-0 on a no-op that looks like success.

## Acceptance — the "no reason to go around" test

An agent runs a real ≥3-lane batch — per-ticket validation, fresh state, liveness, review, merge — using **only** `operator-supervisor` **verbs**: no `node …/adaptive-orchestrator.mjs`, no `operator-run`, no `crabrunner`, no `production-rollout.mjs`, no `SUPERVISOR_*` env vars, no hand-managed capacity/out-dir files. A fresh operator/agent given only `operator-supervisor --help` completes it without trial-and-error or reading source.

## Structure

Sub-issues capture the distinct gaps (capability parity; one invocation surface; clean-slate; vocabulary + safe defaults). Already-filed pieces of the same coherence goal: **MOB-708 / MOB-709** (validation expressible in the front door + executed in the spine), **MOB-707** (heartbeat → live status), **MOB-713** (progress surface / liveness without log archaeology).

## Source

CLI ergonomics evaluation this session across four dogfood logs + the live command surfaces. Current front-door usage: `run` (no `--validation-command`), `continue` (10 flags), the env-var `supervisor-continue` wrapper vs flag `continue`, and long `node …/adaptive-orchestrator.mjs` forms used in practice.

Confirmed as the umbrella for the hand-driving/token-burn mechanism: every lifecycle gap (MOB-778 fresh-init, MOB-799 resume metadata loss, MOB-886 no revalidate-after-repair, MOB-906 group descriptors, MOB-908 gate propagation, MOB-840/846 terminal semantics) pushes orchestrating agents to raw adaptive-orchestrator/crabrunner + polling loops (MOB-774: 10 compactions / 2.63M shell tokens in one dogfood). issues.description:
## Context

During HSMOB-64 session-orchestrator execution in /Users/ericlitman/projects/healthspanners-mobile, the initial worker run produced a valid diff but supervisor validation failed before execution because the generated operator workspace .mise.toml was untrusted. After trusting that workspace, `operator-supervisor continue` did not retry validation, so I tried the documented `operator-supervisor run --resume <run-dir>` path.

The resume row failed immediately with `artifact_missing`: executed operator-run completed without schedule-result.json. The child log said execute was a no-op because scheduled jobs were already complete, with `lease_release.invoked=false` / `reason=not_terminal` and no operation errors. This left the queue with the original validation_failed row and a failed resume row rather than a clean revalidation path.

## Why still real

This can mislead an operator during governed external-repo work: a repairable validation-environment issue becomes a terminal supervisor artifact failure, forcing manual validation and PR handling outside the preferred supervisor path.

## Acceptance criteria

* `operator-supervisor continue` or a documented retry command can rerun requested validation after a validation-environment repair such as `mise trust`.
* `operator-supervisor run --resume <run-dir>` does not emit a failed queue row solely because the underlying schedule is already complete and no schedule-result.json is rewritten.
* If resume cannot revalidate by design, the command returns a clear non-terminal operator instruction instead of `artifact_missing`.
* Regression coverage includes a completed implementation run whose validation initially fails before command execution, then succeeds after an environment repair.

* Reproduce with a run containing `--validation-command scripts/verification-gate` where the operator workspace .mise.toml is initially untrusted.

issues.title: Derive substrate limits from measured data; separate liveness from budget
issues.description:
## Problem

Crucible's numeric limits (timeouts, caps, retry budgets) are guessed constants, patched per symptom, never derived from measured data. Verified inventory on origin/main @ 4bfee1e7 (full table in `docs/plans/2026-07-09-001-triage-root-cause-strategy.md` §7, PR #409):

* crabbox phase timeouts: status **30s**, submit 600s, collect 300s (`crabrunner/src/client.ts:134-137`)
* lane timeout 3600s (`lib/scheduler-timeout.mjs:4`, raised 1800→3600 after MOB-940 — a symptom patch)
* `no_progress_seconds` 600 (`adaptive-orchestrator.mjs:1930`); capacity TTL 300s (`supervisor-frontdoor.mjs:39`)
* EAGAIN sleeps `[250,500,1000,2000]`ms **outside** the phase budget (`client.ts:139,366-388` — MOB-757)
* review-spine backstop 15 rounds (`lib/review-spine.mjs:14`); anthropic maxTurns 24 / codex 20; `turn_cap_reached` is terminal with no continuation (`lane_workers/run.ts:57`)

The turn-cap week (PRs #406/#408) is the exemplar: two classification patches while the budget itself and the at-cap behavior were never measured. Usage-ledger self-usage capture (MOB-1018) landed — the data source exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every limit inventoried with current value + file:line anchor + owner rationale (seed table in strategy doc §7).
- [ ] Distributions pulled from usage ledger / collect archives (lane durations, probe latencies, turn counts at completion vs cap, EAGAIN bursts); proposed values recorded with rationale; enforcement changes ship report-only first (measure-before-caps).
- [ ] Liveness separated from budget: worker progress heartbeats; a quiet-but-alive lane never dies to `no_progress_seconds` (subsumes MOB-873 liveness half, MOB-639 watchdog half).
- [ ] Budget exhaustion (turn cap, wall clock) becomes a recoverable classification with continuation/split path, not terminal-with-no-artifact; MOB-1037's installed-provider turn-cap proof included.
- [ ] EAGAIN sleeps counted inside the phase budget (MOB-757).
